datasheet.title: G6 Intelligent Power Distribution Unit (iPDU) specification sheet PUSP97-WW-ENG 7/2024

description: Panduit P42G20G G6 intelligent rack PDU, monitored and switched per outlet, 0U: a 1780 mm strip for a cabinet's vertical channel. It has a fixed 3 m cord ending in an IEC 60309 3P+E 9h 60 A plug, three-phase delta, 200-240 V. It has 42 outlets in two rows: 21 C13/C15 combination sockets and 21 C13/C15/C19 combination sockets, in six blocks. Each block is on a 20 A double-pole breaker across two of the three lines, as the drawing's labels read. A G6 controller with a display, three buttons, two lamps, five RJ45 jacks and a USB-A port sits between the two halves.

gaps.note: the drawing and Panduit's product page 'P42G20G - Panduit' give 56 by 75 by 1780. The sheet PUSP97 lists a 0U FULL form at 52 by 53 by 1750. The drawing's figures are used.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which form the P42G20G is.

gaps.note: no photograph of any face is held, so no colour, finish, printing or plate shape is checked against a photograph.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of each face of the P42G20G.

gaps.note: no dimension of an outlet or a plate on the front view is stated. The positions are read off the drawing at its own 1780.0 scale.
the drawing prints no outlet numeral that is text, so none is drawn. The numbering is column by column from the cord end.
gaps.wanted: a front view whose outlet numerals are text.

gaps.note: the 10 A 'C13/C15 COMBO' socket is a C13 outlet with the C15 extension its name states. It presents the C13 key and no C15 plug is registered. The 16 A socket presents the combination key. The drawing dimensions neither.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the socket.

gaps.note: the sheet draws the plug end-on at the left of the front view and in its PLUG block. The reused cord part draws no plug face, so the bottom face is the cord gland alone.
gaps.wanted: a cord part that draws the plug face.

gaps.note: the rear view's callout names twelve toolless button locations, and the view draws two buttons. No document says where the other ten are.
the dot lattices, screws, tabs, window and corner marks of the sides and the far end are drawn from the sheet as unnamed decor. No document names any of them. The far end's flange tabs are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of each long side.

gaps.note: the breaker plates are drawn about 56 along the strip against panduit/g5-breaker-20a's 70.2. The part is reused and the plates are placed on their drawn centres.
the front view's second row of labels pairs B3 [WHITE] with the second block and B1 [DARK GRAY] with the third. The row above pairs B1, B2 and B3 with the blocks in order, and that row is used.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of each block's colour.

gaps.note: the earth symbol of the cord-end plate, the boxed 1/2 on each block, the rating triangles and the small boxes are not drawn. The breaker legends and the controller's wordmark are drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the cord end and a block.

gaps.note: Panduit's product page 'P42G20G - Panduit' lists 'Green LED indicates outlet is on'. No held picture shows the lamp, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the outlet face.

gaps.note: sheet 2 of the drawing lists the plain P42G20G only; its key lists six colours, three cord lengths and a bottom-end-fed cord. The device states the plain part's 3 m cord and 11.5 kg only.
gaps.wanted: an order for each variant that has a held photograph or a dimensioned drawing.

breakers.description: six 20 A double-pole breakers, B1 to B6, each feeding one block of outlets

outlets.mixed: the PDU's 42 outlets, numbered 1 to 42 column by column from the cord end - 21 C13/C15 and 21 C13/C15/C19 combination sockets, each switchable

name: p42g20g

banks.note: drawing - the front view labels the six blocks with a colour each. They read 'B1 [DARK GRAY]', 'B2 [LIGHT GRAY]' and 'B3 [WHITE]', then 'B4 [DARK GRAY]', 'B5 [LIGHT GRAY]' and 'B6 [WHITE]'. The labels sit above the blocks, left to right from the cord end. A second row of labels below the blocks pairs B3 with the second block and B1 with the third (gaps: bank-colour-labels). The six breaker plates are B1 to B6, each printing its lines: L1-L2, L2-L3, L3-L1, L1-L2, L2-L3, L3-L1. THAT BLOCK Bk IS FED BY BREAKER Bk IS A READING OF THE LABELS. The three greys are drawn as #55585c, #9a9da1 and #e4e5e7 and are estimates of the words.

capability.note: drawing - the unit type is MONITORED & SWITCHED PER OUTLET. So `metering-scope: outlet` and `outlet-switching: true`.

chassis.note: drawing - 1780.0 long (front view) and 56.0 and 75.0 on the bottom view. Panduit's product page 'P42G20G - Panduit' prints 56 mm wide, 1,780 mm high and 75 mm deep, and agrees. The sheet PUSP97 lists a 0U FULL form at 52 by 53 by 1750 and no form at 1780 (gaps: body-size). The drawing's figures are used. Weight 11.5 kg is on sheet 2's part table only.

colour.note: drawing - sheet 2 gives BLACK (RAL 9005) for the plain part number P42G20G. It is drawn here as the RAL's #0e0e10 on the body. THE PLATE, MOULDING AND SCREW COLOURS ARE NOT CHECKED against any source. No photograph is held, so no colour is sampled.

controller.note: drawing - the controller plate is drawn between the blank plate and the fourth breaker plate, about 142 along against the component's 127.8. The bay is centred on it. P42G20G is composed with panduit/g6-controller@1 in a bay because the sheet PUSP97 calls the controller hot swappable. The part names each jack by the label the plate prints.

ends.note: ESTIMATED from the vector paths. The sheet's BOTTOM VIEW is the far end, the library's top face. It holds a 10 by 10 lattice of 100 dots on a 4.96 mm pitch, placed to about 2 mm. Its flange tabs are not drawn (gaps: side-marks). The sheet draws the cord's plug end-on at the left of the front view and in its PLUG block. The reused cord part has no plug face, so the bottom face is the cord gland alone (gaps: cord-end-face).

front.note: drawing - the front view. From the cord end: a plate with the external ground, three breaker plates B1 to B3, and three blocks of four columns of two outlets. Then come a blank plate with five hexagon-head marks and a ring, the controller and breaker plates B4 to B6. The marks sit in a 2, 1, 2 layout along the plate. Three blocks of three columns run to the far end. Plate, block and outlet positions match the P42G20M's to 1 mm, checked against the 300 dpi rendering. The outlet pitch is not dimensioned. The column pitch is 37.1 in the first half, as on the P42G20M, and kept in the second.

input.note: drawing - 'INPUT PLUG: IEC 60309 3P+E (IP44)' and plug 'IEC 60309, 3P 4W, 9H'. It also prints 'INPUT VOLTAGE: 200-240VAC' and 'INPUT CURRENT: 60A (48A DERATED)'. It prints 'INPUT PHASE: THREE-PHASE, DELTA' and 'RATED POWER: 17.3 kVA'. Sheet 2 gives the plain part number a 3 m cord. The cord is one part at the cord end; its length and the plug's face are not drawn.

lamps.note: datasheet - Panduit's product page 'P42G20G - Panduit' lists 'Green LED indicates outlet is on'. That is a green LED per outlet. No held picture shows the lamp and the outlet parts carry none, so none is drawn on the strip (gaps: outlet-lamps). No photograph is held, so no lit colour is sampled.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S VECTOR DRAWING. Panduit customer drawing P42G20G-XXYZ_DC rev 00A (11/03/2023), two sheets, has a front, rear, left, right and bottom view. Its scale was taken from its own 1780.0 overall dimension, which is 609.9 pt on the sheet, so 2.918 mm to the point. The 1555.0 between the buttons agrees. Positions were read off renderings of the front view at 200 and 300 dpi and off the vector paths, to about 1 mm. The library draws the PDU STANDING, cord end down, so a position along the drawing becomes 1780 minus that, and a position across becomes x. No photograph and no 3D model of the part is held.

mount.note: `rack-side`: the strip stands beside a rack's upright on two mounting buttons on its back, 1555.0 apart and 40.5 from the cord end (rear view). The drawing says 'VERTICAL, 0U FULL' and gives no count of units. `ru: 40` is the whole units the 1780 mm length covers (40.04), and no held page states it.

outlets.note: drawing - '(21)C13/C15, (21)C13/C15/C19'. The receptacle block draws each as ONE SOCKET named 'C13/C15 COMBO 10A' and 'C13/C15/C19 COMBO 16A', so each is one outlet. The sheet PUSP97 prints the second as C13/C15/C19/C21. The upper row of the front view is the C13/C15 and the lower row the C13/C15/C19 (x = 4 and 28). The outlets are numbered 1 to 42 column by column from the cord end, the upper socket first. THE NUMBERING IS AN ASSUMPTION, as the drawing prints no outlet numeral (gaps: outlet-numerals). THE WAY UP OF EACH SOCKET IS NOT READ.

rear.note: drawing - the rear view: two buttons 40.5 from the cord end and 1555.0 apart, on the strip's centre line. Two marks 5.5 across sit 24.0 from the buttons, as the view's 24.0 dimensions read. A 7.1 ring sits near the far end. The callout 'TOOLESS MOUNTING BUTTON LOCATIONS (12) PL' names twelve locations, and the view draws the two buttons and no other (gaps: rear-marks).

sides.note: ESTIMATED from the vector paths of sheet 1 (2.918 mm to the point, scaled on the 1780.0 overall dimension). The sheet stacks FRONT, RIGHT, REAR and LEFT upward and puts BOTTOM beside FRONT, as the P42G20M's sheet does. The library stands the strip cord end down, a half turn in the plane. The sheet's RIGHT VIEW is the library's left face and its LEFT VIEW the library's right face. The pairs of marks 24.0 apart agree in both views. Dot lattices: RIGHT VIEW holds 1748 closed 0.6 pt marks, 1.75 mm across. One is drawn twice, so 1747 dots in 17 blocks on a 4.96 mm pitch. LEFT VIEW holds 1659 dots in 16 blocks on the same pitch. Counted twice, by bounding box and by distinct centres. Also drawn: 12 and 24 round screws 7.1 across, and four marks 5.5 across in two pairs 24.0 apart on each face. Each face also has 42 small tabs along its outlet-side edge. The LEFT VIEW's window is 157.6 by 32.1, with two corner marks. Each position is good to about 1 mm. No function is stated for any mark.
